skills.name: canonify
skills.description: How to operate Canonify declaratively. SKILL.md is the map: auth and CLI rules, the authoring loop, the envelope and runtime frame, the audit trail, and which companion skill owns each topic.

skills.name: canonify-app-authoring
skills.description: A short, top-to-bottom tutorial that takes an empty Canon org to a working app: schema.propose_migration → catalog.refine_object_type → actions.declare → state_machines.register → view_specs.declare, one example per chapter, each linking to its one reference page in canonify-objects-actions or canonify-viewspecs. Covers the approval path for agent-authored declarations, seeding with objects.import, verifying the rendered app, a complete worked-example bundle with its scenario, app patterns (human codes, create-then-transition, bookings and weekly series), the App record and the catalog bundle lifecycle, and bilingual apps.

skills.name: canonify-app-lifecycle
skills.description: When to stop adding surface. The five lifecycle rules for a Canonify canon: take one app to a real 1.0 before starting the next, define 1.0 as three to five falsifiable conditions (usually a replay of a closed period, not a live parallel run against a system users keep editing), park unfinished work out of the app nav instead of deleting it, run the retained catalog audit and structural validation before calling anything done, and verify every nav or ViewSpec change in the rendered app rather than in a test suite. Read when you are handed a brief bigger than one app, or before you declare your second app.

skills.name: canonify-domain-modelling
skills.description: The four obligations every Canonify domain model must meet, each stated as a rule with a worked before/after: reuse the canonical object instead of retyping its name into text columns (C1-shadow-entity), declare the upward link over every FK column, check the platform catalog before modelling a capability it already ships, and model time and money as effective-dated append-only rows with snapshotted settlements and integer minor units (C10-float-money). The other skills teach the mechanics; this one states what is obligatory. Read after the base `canonify` skill and before your first migration.

skills.name: canonify-esign-sender
skills.description: A reference ViewSpec catalog for the Canon-customer e-signature SENDER surface: a creator-scoped sent-agreements table (title + status + decline_reason, with a per-row void), plus a create form for new signing envelopes. Distributed as an on-disk catalog.apply bundle (views + policies only) that composes the PLATFORM signature_envelope object-type and the signature_envelope.create/.void actions already present in every canon — nothing is baked into the empty canon. Apply it on demand with `canon catalog apply`.

skills.name: canonify-isomorphism
skills.description: Why REST, CLI, and MCP are three isomorphic projections of one Canon catalog — the runtime contract they all call, the envelope they all return, why they can't drift, and how to debug 'works on CLI but not REST'. Read SKILL.md first, then deep-dive on the runtime contract or connecting an MCP client.

skills.name: canonify-objects-actions
skills.description: The reference for Canonify's catalog mechanics: tables and auto-CRUD, bulk import, ObjectTypes (properties, enums, display, visibility, temporal), links and compound objects, ActionTypes (input, governance, idempotency, presentation), the handler DSL, state machines, schedules, and the built-in e-signature and outbox actions. Every JSON example decodes against the live validators. Read after the base `canonify` skill.

skills.name: canonify-scenarios
skills.description: How to write + run declarative Canonify scenarios (session.yaml) that prove an app slice end-to-end through the public Canon surface — live verification, not jsdom mocking. Read SKILL.md first (it covers running and reading failures), then the structure reference and the patterns.

skills.name: canonify-viewspecs
skills.description: Author Canonify ViewSpecs — the declarative UI primitive. Compose catalog pieces (ObjectTypes + ActionTypes) into transport-agnostic views built from 11 block types (table, detail, panel, button, composite, metric, chart, file, board, calendar, queue), then declare them to an org via view_specs.declare. Read SKILL.md first, then the cheatsheet.
